$header_note: QPB v1.5.7 post-172 BUG-009 retest — 6 claude/haiku runs validating that the schedule-then-collect contract is end-to-end honored after the 167-172 stack landed. Pool=2 matches the current default anthropic cap so the test runs with NO CLI overrides (no --max-per-provider). v1.5.7 174 (queued, currently halted at scope review) will delete the cap subsystem entirely and pool becomes the only knob; this plan is forward-compatible with that change. The 3-repo × 2-channel matrix gives 6 total runs at pool=2: 2 spawn immediately; 4 starve at orchestrator launch and write PENDING manifest entries (161-A); as each of the first 2 finishes (haiku ≈ 5-7 min), 171's on-terminate retry path spawns the next PENDING entry; the 172 BUG-009 fix ensures retry-spawned futures are actually submitted for collection (pre-172 the formerly-PENDING idx was wrongly in collected_indices). Expected: all 6 grade cleanly in one collector lifetime across 3 batches of 2, no manual `collect` invocations, watchdog quiet throughout (no orphans expected; watchdog deadlock from 172 FINDING-1 is dormant on the happy path).

runs.description: Row 1 — claude/haiku reviews gson via pip-local-wheel (Mode A). Cheap-tier across the pip channel; expect ~5-7 min runtime; first batch.
Row 2 — claude/haiku reviews gson via npm-local-tgz (Mode A). Same repo + npm channel; exercises the npx --yes / --prefer-offline install path under haiku.
Row 3 — claude/haiku reviews Express via pip-local-wheel (Mode A). Different repo (Node ecosystem); pip channel.
Row 4 — claude/haiku reviews Express via npm-local-tgz (Mode A). Different repo from rows 1-2; npm channel.
Row 5 — claude/haiku reviews chi via pip-local-wheel (Mode A). Go ecosystem; pip channel; third distinct repo for variance in finish times.
Row 6 — claude/haiku reviews chi via npm-local-tgz (Mode A). Same repo as row 5 + npm channel; rounds out the 3-repo × 2-channel matrix.
